newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain EconMin details Feb budget data. [CORRECTED 12:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Spain EconMin details Feb budget data. [CORRECTED 12:27 GMT]

text.p: The Economy Ministry said the central government budget, on a national account basis, was in deficit (corrects to read deficit, not surplus) in February by 286.5 billion pesetas from a provisional deficit of 399.5 billion pesetas in January.
It added that on a cash basis the central government budget was in surplus by 176.2 billion pesetas from a deficit of 376.5 billion pesetas in January.
The Economy Ministry said there was a primary surplus of 688.6 billion pesetas in February alone, and for the two months to February the figure was in surplus to the tune of 652.0 billion pesetas.

NOTE - The figures relate to central government finances only. GBR = government borrowing requirement, or provisional surplus/deficit on a national account basis.

The central government public deficit on a national account basis is the one considered relevant for the Maastricht Treaty, which sets out the economic requirements that must be met to join the European single currency launch.
It takes into account accrued revenues and expenditures for a given period, while the deficit on a cash basis registers actual money movements during a given month.
